slides: Frame the chapter as a warning about nuisance geometry. The target parameter may be low-dimensional, but inference can be distorted when every new observation group brings another nuisance direction. The geometric question is which component of the data variation still points cleanly toward the target.

Use this route slide to keep several statistical topics on one map. Nuisance fibers set the geometry, the Neyman-Scott experiment shows a failure mode, estimating functions repair it through orthogonality, and semiparametric projection generalizes the same idea to function-valued nuisance directions.

The nuisance-fiber picture is deliberately low-dimensional. Fixing the target coordinate leaves a fiber of nuisance values, and the Neyman-Scott setting keeps adding new fibers as the sample grows. More data therefore do not automatically mean the target direction becomes easier to isolate.

The Neyman-Scott slide should feel concrete. With two observations per group, the profile likelihood plugs in every group mean and leaves only half the variance in the residuals. The sanity file confirms the profile mean near 0.5 while the estimating equation stays near the true value 1.0.

Estimating functions are geometric objects, not merely algebraic tricks. A valid rule has mean zero at the target, but an efficient rule also removes nuisance components. The figure shows the target score decomposed into nuisance projection plus the horizontal residual used for inference.

Semiparametric projection is the same operation in a larger space. The target score is a curve, the nuisance tangent space is spanned by basis directions, and the efficient score is the residual after projection. The numerical inner products verify that residual orthogonality is essentially exact.

The spike-interval example turns nuisance into a time-local diagnostic. Short intervals cluster where the background rate rises, so an apparent signal can be created by nuisance rate variation. This slide is a caution: visual bursts require an estimating rule that separates background from target.

Use the applied lab to compare estimators across group sizes. The profile estimator follows the theoretical bias curve m minus one over m, while the corrected estimating rule remains centered near one. Students can see that larger groups reduce the issue but do not change the geometry.

This synthesis slide pulls the lesson away from the special example. Likelihood is not rejected; it is inspected. When nuisance directions are stable, ordinary asymptotics can work, but when those directions grow or become infinite-dimensional, horizontal projection and estimating equations become the safer language.

Close with the checks because they make the abstract geometry auditable. The profile estimator matches the half-limit for m equals two, efficient scores are orthogonal to nuisance directions, the semiparametric residual is orthogonal to the basis, and all artifact files exist for inspection.
